description: Find sprints that were disbanded — deleted, or emptied in one go — by reading the issues' history: the issues whose sprint went from X to nothing by the same person within a minute of each other, at least two of them. source='here' (the default) reads this tracker's history — for a sprint deleted before the trash existed, purged from it, or emptied by a bulk move; a sprint still in the trash is named with state 'trash' and is brought back by restore_sprint, which knows more. source='jira' reads the project's linked Jira (get_jira_connection): the changelog's Sprint field of the Jira project's issues updated in the window, on the project's token — one of your 10 reads of the linked Jira a minute. Each candidate: 'id' (what rebuild_sprint takes), 'sprint' (name; state deleted — gone; open — still there, the issues go back into it; trash; unknown), 'at' / 'until', 'by', 'issues' (how many), and where each is now: 'free' (in the backlog — these go back), 'in' (already in that sprint), 'elsewhere' (in another sprint, which stays — with where), 'gone' and 'hidden' counted. 'canRebuild' says whether you may rebuild it. A completed sprint is not a disband and is not listed.

from.description: From when, YYYY-MM-DD or a moment with its zone. Default: 90 days ago; at most a year before 'to'.

jiraProject.description: With source='jira': the Jira project's key, e.g. 'ACME'. Default: the one most of this project's linked issues are in.

projectKey.description: Project key here whose board's sprints to look for, e.g. 'PM'.

source.description: 'here' (the default) or 'jira' — the project's linked Jira.

sprint.description: Only this sprint name (exact, any case).

name: find_lost_sprints
title: Find lost sprints
